summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR712 crore and operating margin held at 10.44%, though Q2 gross margin fell to 16-17%.
summary.overview: Dynamic Cables reported H1 FY27 revenue of INR712 crore (up 31% YoY), operating profit of INR74.3 crore (up 29%) at a 10.44% margin, and PAT of INR47.1 crore (up 24%). Management attributed the Q2 gross margin decline to product and order mix plus some commodity volatility, and said volume growth was about 6% in the quarter, with the rest of growth from price. The new manufacturing plant's machinery is installed and is expected to contribute from H2 FY27, with a ramp-up over 3-4 quarters. Management reiterated 10-11% EBITDA margin and sub-15%-of-EBITDA finance cost guidance and a long-term ~20% value growth CAGR.

segments.name: High tension cables
segments.commentary: About 65% of Q2 sales and roughly two-thirds on a broader basis; management says mix moves only 2-3% quarter to quarter.

segments.name: Low tension cables
segments.commentary: About 28% of Q2 sales; 25-30% on a broader basis.

segments.name: Conductors and other products
segments.commentary: About 7% of Q2 sales; 8-10% on a broader basis.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guided at 10-11%, which management says is maintainable going forward; no quantitative margin guidance beyond that.
Finance cost to stay below 15% of EBITDA, including the new facility; six-month figure is about 10-11%.
New plant revenue potential of about INR240-250 crore at 6-7x asset turn on a INR40-45 crore investment, with ramp-up over 3-4 quarters from H2 FY27.
Long-term value growth guidance of around 20% CAGR reiterated; management declined to give a FY27 or FY28 growth number, saying H1 price growth was high so it was being cautious.
Order book expected to see meaningful growth over the next 4-5 quarters as new plant orders optimise.
capex_capacity: New manufacturing facility: plant and machinery installed; expected to contribute from H2 FY27.
Investment in new plant about INR40-45 crore; revenue potential INR240-250 crore at 6-7x asset turn.

Gross block about INR200 crore (INR184 crore at March 2026 plus INR10-15 crore capitalised in H1), implying existing capacity revenue of about INR1,400-1,500 crore at 7x, subject to 10-15% price-driven variation.
Company has no specific term debt for the new plant; described as debt-free on a long-term basis, with finance cost driven by working capital and vendor financing.
Management says capex will be ongoing, with brownfield or greenfield expansions announced from time to time.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 6% in Q2; management says demand is value-driven and latent T&D demand is large.
Management expects overall value growth of around 20% CAGR long term.
Raw material price pass-through: 80-90% of contracts have price variation clauses; fixed-price contracts are under 20% of the book.
Exports are about 7-8% of order book; US shipments were weak in the quarter due to high sea freight and insurance costs and tariff concerns.
Order booking has improved, per management, and is expected to improve further as aluminium prices correct; aluminium cited at falling from about INR3,800 to INR3,000 per analyst.
Top 10 customers contribute about 40-45% of sales; 70-80% of sales come from repeat customers on a yearly basis.
Management says no impact seen so far from UltraTech's entry (UltraVolt), with housewire the most exposed segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in finance cost despite falling quarter-end borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finance cost is levied on average working capital utilisation plus vendor financing charges; it is not linked to the new plant, and six-month finance cost is about 10-11% of EBITDA, with a stated ceiling of 15%.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue can the new facility generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment of INR40-45 crore at 6-7x asset turn implies INR240-250 crore revenue potential, ramping over 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline to 16-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product and order mix shifts quarter to quarter and some commodity volatility, which is largely passed through; the margin decline was not due to commodity inflation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was about 6% in Q2; management declined to split value growth into price and volume beyond this, and said EBITDA per ton is not the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 20% long-term value growth but gave no quantitative FY27 or FY28 guidance, citing caution after high H1 price growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there competitive impact from UltraTech's entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact has been seen so far from UltraVolt; it noted housewire is the segment most likely to be affected first.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure in Q2 (16-17%) from mix and commodity volatility; watch whether EBITDA stays within 10-11%.
Volume growth of about 6% versus price-led value growth; sustainability of volume recovery as aluminium prices move.
Export weakness from freight, insurance and tariff issues, particularly the US market.
Ramp-up timing of the new plant over 3-4 quarters and order book growth over the next 4-5 quarters.
Working capital intensity: inventory higher in H1 ahead of H2 seasonality, with receivables under 60 days.
Data centre and electron beam solar cable products still in development; no timeline given for data centre cables.
Competitive intensity from UltraTech's entry, especially in housewire.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and margin range, but cautious and evasive on quantitative FY27/FY28 guidance, volume split and export timing. Management repeatedly deflected questions on volume versus price and margin drivers to value-based framing.
key_quotes: So, the total investment in the plant is around 40-45 crores.
On operating profit levels, we have guided always, maintained our guidance of 10% to 11%, EBITDA percentage.
So, nothing specific to do with, commodity price inflation.
Only, there are 10%-20% contracts which are on fixed price basis.
